messages:
PagerDuty Bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected: paging surge on runtime-prod-uswest-1 - increased OOM/paging events on gpu-pool-3.  p95 tail-latency > 2s, token fail rate up. Auto-runbook: <https://playbooks.redwood.internal/paging>|runbook> triggered. thread_ts=2799999999

Emma (oncall): I'm on it. assigning to @Raj and @Mike. first check: which model rollout or traffic pattern changed in the last 2h?

Raj (runtime): seeing spikes correlated with a rollout of `gpt-open-1-8bit` that started ~16900s ago (automated canary). Canary increased batched requests (avg batch_size 12 -> 18). Hypothesis: larger batches + longer contexts -> heavier KV-cache residency -> fragmentation/paging.

Mike (infra): Confirmed host-level memory pressure on GPU nodes in pool `gpu-pool-3`. Paging to host (NVMe) observed. Not full node OOM yet but swap activity high. Will pull `nvidia-smi` snapshots.

Raj (runtime): Paste `nvidia-smi` snapshot for gpu-07:```
Tue Mar 12 14:02:11 2025
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| Fan  Temp  Perf  Pwr:Usage/Cap|         Memory-Usage | GPU-Util  Compute M. |
| 07   A100-SXM4       On       | 00000000:84:00.0 Off |                    0 |
| 30%   68C    P2   170W / 400W |   61.20GiB / 80.00GiB |     98%      C   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+```
Fragmentation metrics: slab pages ~ 11,800 (hot), free contiguous pages small. KV-cache residency per model shard ~ 22GB.

Emma (oncall): Customer impact? which customers hit 5xx or degraded latency?

Olivia (cust-succ): CS reports 6 customers with elevated error rates; 2 on enterprise Dedicated plans reported timeouts for sync endpoints (IDs C-9201, C-9442). Notified via status page. No payment-impacting SLA breaches yet but close.

Raj (runtime): Live logs showing OOM-ish traces from runtime allocator:```
[2025-03-12T14:01:58Z] ERROR runtime: allocate_kv_segment failed: requested 6144KB, contiguous_free_pages=0, fragmentation_threshold_exceeded
[2025-03-12T14:02:01Z] WARN rpc: downstream request failed: context deadline exceeded
```
Probable causes: (1) KV cache growth due to longer contexts, (2) larger batches increasing peak allocation, (3) allocator unable to coalesce fragments -> paging.

Emma (oncall): Immediate mitigations to reduce customer impact — propose: roll back canary or throttle batch sizes, increase aggressive eviction (kv.eviction_policy=aggressive), and route heavy customers to dedicated capacity. Which is fastest?

Mike (infra): Fastest = throttle at ingress LB (set max_batch_size=8 for the model route) and enable `kv_eviction=aggressive` via runtime flag - takes ~30s to apply rolling config. Rolling rollback of model canary will need ~4-6m. I'll apply throttle + eviction now.

Raj (runtime): Also enable prefix/KV-cache warmup disabled for canary to free transient entries. Command:```bash
# set runtime config to throttle and eviction
redwoodctl routes update runtime-prod-uswest-1 --model gpt-open-1-8bit --max-batch-size 8 --kv-eviction aggressive
```
Applying now.

InfraBot: Config change applied to 12/12 nodes in gpu-pool-3. Rolling restart of runtime workers queued.

Emma (oncall): Observability: augment token-level tracing and enable debug logs for 15m to capture timeline. Raj - pull pre/post old logs and annotate timeline. Olivia - send quick ping to affected customers that we're mitigating and expecting improvement within 10m.

Olivia (cust-succ): Notifying customers now — message drafted and sent to C-9201 & C-9442. Updating status page with mitigation steps.

Raj (runtime): Post-mitigation stats after throttle+eviction (5m later): p95 latency back to baseline ~420ms, token fail rate down 70%, GPU free memory ~72GiB/80GiB on most nodes. New `nvidia-smi` snippet:```
GPU07 Mem: 33.8GiB / 80.0GiB, Util 42%
```
No obvious OOMs after change. Looks effective.

Emma (oncall): Good. We're stabilizing. Will keep monitoring for 30m. Hypotheses to track in RCA thread: 1) Canary increased average batch size causing peak KV allocations; 2) Allocator fragmentation prevented coalescing -> forced NVMe paging under pressure; 3) Model variant `gpt-open-1-8bit` increased per-token KV usage vs previous model. Need logs, waveform of batch sizes, shard residency over time.

SRE Lead: Taking over next shift at 15:00UTC. Emma, capture timeline + logs + exact config changes (commands & who ran them). Also collect kernel slab/alloc histograms and the runtime allocator debug dump. I'll create an RCA doc.

Emma (oncall): Handoff: summary -> mitigation applied (throttle -> max_batch_size 8, kv_eviction aggressive, disabled prefix warmup, rollback withheld), observed recovery in 5m, impacted customers notified. Hypotheses listed above. Links: runbook <https://playbooks.redwood.internal/paging>, config change audit <https://infra-audit.local/chgs/8932>, log bundle: <https://logs.redwood/internal/2799999999>|logs>.

SRE Lead: Thanks. Next actions for RCA: - collect histograms and full `kubectl logs --since=2h` for affected pods - reproduce in staging with aggressive fragmentation (simulate high batch+long ctx) - evaluate allocator patch (coalescing heuristic) and model quantization differences. Assign Raj and Mike.

Emma (oncall): tagging this thread with `incident:paging` and `rca:needed`. Passing to SRE Lead for follow-up.

Customer Success Bot: Noted 2 customers affected, both replied acknowledging mitigation. No escalations required.

SRE Lead: Logged RCA ticket IR-2025-314. Will update with timeline + hypotheses + remediation plan. Closing live incident channel in 30m if stable.
